info.name: S3 API
info.summary: Expose Nextcloud folders as S3-compatible buckets
info.description:
**Point any S3 client at a Nextcloud folder.**
Mark a folder as a bucket in your personal settings, create an API key, and use it with the AWS CLI, boto3, rclone or any other S3-compatible client. The files stay ordinary Nextcloud files — visible in the web UI, synced by the desktop client, shareable, versioned. Nothing is duplicated into a separate object store.
Rather than the handful of calls a file sync needs, this implements the parts that make an S3 endpoint usable as a real backend:
* Conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) that serialise concurrent writers, so the store works as a compare-and-swap primitive * Multipart uploads, including `UploadPartCopy` for server-side compose * Ranged and conditional reads, delimited listings, presigned URLs * Streaming uploads — bodies are never buffered in memory, and `aws-chunked` payloads have their per-chunk signature chain verified * Correct S3 ETags (content MD5, compound form for multipart) rather than Nextcloud's internal etag, which is too coarse to build a compare-and-swap on
Authentication is AWS Signature V4, via header or presigned URL. Each API key is scoped to exactly one bucket and is either readonly or readwrite.
Verified against [walgit](https://github.com/tobi/walgit)'s store contract suite, which exercises compare-and-swap under 32-way concurrency, ranged reads, delimited listings and multipart round trips.
**Note:** every request passes through PHP and Nextcloud's storage layer. This is a convenient way to talk S3 to data you already keep in Nextcloud — not a replacement for a high-throughput object store.
info.author: Markus Bergholz
